strings.d1.s0.name: Hosier Lane
strings.d1.s0.tips: A graffiti lane that changes daily, next to ACDC Lane.
strings.d1.s1.name: Degraves Street Breakfast
strings.d1.s1.tips: Laneway cafes serving flat whites and avocado toast, near Centre Place.
strings.d1.s2.name: State Library Victoria La Trobe Reading Room
strings.d1.s2.tips: An octagonal reading room, free to enter. Look out for Ned Kelly's armour.
strings.d1.s3.name: Federation Square & ACMI
strings.d1.s3.tips: ACMI, the film museum, is free. The Ian Potter NGV showcases Australian art, and the Yarra riverbank is right there.
strings.d1.s4.name: Lune Croissanterie Fitzroy
strings.d1.s4.tips: Billed as the world's best croissant. Take tram 11 to Fitzroy and expect a queue.
strings.d1.b0.name: Higher Ground Breakfast
strings.d1.b0.tips: Brunch in a former power station on Little Bourke Street.
strings.d1.b1.name: Melbourne Museum Carlton
strings.d1.b1.tips: Natural history and an Aboriginal gallery, next to the Royal Exhibition Building. A swap for ACMI.
strings.d2.s0.name: Queen Victoria Market
strings.d2.s0.tips: A market dating from 1878. Try the American Doughnut Kitchen van and the cheese and deli hall. The summer night market runs on Wednesdays. Closed Monday and Wednesday.
strings.d2.s1.name: Royal Exhibition Building & Carlton Gardens
strings.d2.s1.tips: A UNESCO-listed exhibition hall from 1880, with fountains and gardens.
strings.d2.s2.name: Lygon Street
strings.d2.s2.tips: Little Italy: Brunetti pastry shop and Pellegrini's, where Melbourne's coffee scene began.
strings.d2.s3.name: Fitzroy Brunswick Street
strings.d2.s3.tips: Vintage shops, street art and the Rose Street Artists' Market at weekends.
strings.d2.s4.name: Naked for Satan Rooftop Bar
strings.d2.s4.tips: A Fitzroy rooftop with city sunset views and pintxos.
strings.d2.b0.name: Pellegrini's Espresso Bar
strings.d2.b0.tips: An espresso bar unchanged since 1954, on Bourke Street.
strings.d2.b1.name: Melbourne Zoo
strings.d2.b1.tips: A zoo in Royal Park. A swap for Fitzroy if you're travelling with children.
strings.d3.s0.name: Bells Beach
strings.d3.s0.tips: Take a tour leaving at 06:30 (130 AUD) or drive. A legendary surf beach at Torquay.
strings.d3.s1.name: Kennett River Koala Walk
strings.d3.s1.tips: Wild koalas and parrots in the trees, along Grey River Road.
strings.d3.s2.name: Apollo Bay
strings.d3.s2.tips: A fishing town known for fish and chips and calamari.
strings.d3.s3.name: Twelve Apostles
strings.d3.s3.tips: Limestone stacks (8 remain). Gibson Steps lead 86 steps down to the beach. The light is best in the afternoon.
strings.d3.s4.name: Loch Ard Gorge
strings.d3.s4.tips: A shipwreck cove with caves, 3 minutes from the Apostles. Allow 3 hours for the return.
strings.d3.b0.name: Cape Otway Lightstation
strings.d3.b0.tips: The oldest lighthouse on mainland Australia. A swap for Apollo Bay.
strings.d3.b1.name: Apollo Bay Bakery
strings.d4.s0.name: Brighton Bathing Boxes
strings.d4.s0.tips: 82 colourful huts on Dendy Street Beach. Take the train to Middle Brighton. Quiet in the morning.
strings.d4.s1.name: St Kilda Esplanade & Pier
strings.d4.s1.tips: Take tram 96 to the pier and the Luna Park laughing mouth. Little penguins appear at sunset (under the pier).
strings.d4.s2.name: Acland Street Cake Shops
strings.d4.s2.tips: Monarch Cakes (1934) and European patisseries, a legacy of Jewish immigrants.
strings.d4.s3.name: Luna Park Melbourne
strings.d4.s3.tips: A funfair from 1912. Entry is free, and the Scenic Railway wooden roller coaster costs 15 AUD.
strings.d4.s4.name: St Kilda Pier Penguins
strings.d4.s4.tips: Little penguins on the breakwater at sunset. No flash photography, and volunteers are on hand.
strings.d4.b0.name: Stokehouse St Kilda
strings.d4.b0.tips: A stylish restaurant right on the beach.
strings.d4.b1.name: Jewish Museum of Australia
strings.d4.b1.tips: St Kilda's Jewish museum. A swap for the garden.
strings.d5.s0.name: Brighton to Phillip Island and Churchill Island
strings.d5.s0.tips: Take a tour leaving at 12:00 (130 AUD, penguins included) or drive for 2 hours. See the historic farm and a sheep shearing show.
strings.d5.s1.name: Koala Conservation Reserve
strings.d5.s2.name: Cape Woolamai Coastal Walk
strings.d5.s2.tips: A pink granite headland and surf beach, with the Pinnacles.
strings.d5.s3.name: The Nobbies & Seal Rocks
strings.d5.s3.tips: Rocky cliffs, seagull colonies and fur seals. Bring binoculars.
strings.d5.s4.name: Penguin Parade
strings.d5.s4.tips: At sunset, thousands of little penguins waddle from the sea to their burrows. Book tickets online. Photography is NOT allowed, and bring a coat.
strings.d5.b0.name: Penguin Parade Cafe
strings.d5.b0.tips: In the visitor centre, serving fish and soup.
strings.d5.b1.name: Panny's Chocolate Factory
strings.d5.b1.tips: A chocolate factory. A swap for the koalas if you're travelling with children.
strings.d6.s0.name: Yarra Valley Dairy
strings.d6.s1.name: Domaine Chandon Yarra Valley
strings.d6.s1.tips: Sparkling wine tasting with vineyard views. Take a tour (about 150 AUD) or drive for 1 hour.
strings.d6.s2.name: Healesville Sanctuary
strings.d6.s2.tips: Native animals including kangaroos, platypuses and wombats, plus a bird show.
strings.d6.s3.name: Yering Station
strings.d6.s3.tips: A winery on a historic farm, with pinot noir and views.
strings.d6.b0.name: TarraWarra Estate
strings.d6.b0.tips: Wine plus an art museum. A swap for Yering.
strings.d6.b1.name: Innocent Bystander Healesville
strings.d6.b1.tips: Pizza and wine in the town centre.
strings.d7.s0.name: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria
strings.d7.s0.tips: 38 hectares of gardens, with the Ornamental Lake and views of the Shrine of Remembrance.
strings.d7.s1.name: Shrine of Remembrance
strings.d7.s1.tips: See the city from the memorial balcony. Free entry.
strings.d7.s2.name: Southbank Promenade
strings.d7.s2.tips: The Yarra riverbank. Eureka Skydeck (30 AUD) is optional.
strings.d7.s3.name: Southgate Breakfast-Lunch
strings.d7.s3.tips: Riverside views and a farewell flat white.
strings.d7.s4.name: Southern Cross SkyBus
strings.d7.s4.tips: SkyBus to Tullamarine takes 30 minutes. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Eureka Skydeck
strings.d7.b0.tips: The 88th floor and the Edge glass box.
strings.d7.b1.name: Ponyfish Island
strings.d7.b1.tips: A floating bar-cafe under the bridge.
strings.note0: Buy a myki at 7-Eleven. The centre is a Free Tram Zone, and the SkyBus airport transfer costs 22 AUD. For the Great Ocean Road, Phillip Island and Yarra Valley, take a tour or hire a car (they drive on the left).
strings.note1: December to February is summer at 25-35°C, with hot northerly winds bringing 40°C days. The Australian Open is in January and the F1 in March. March to May, in autumn, is best.
strings.note2: Coffee culture is among the world's best: try a flat white or a magic. Brunch costs 25-30 AUD and tours 130-150 AUD. Tipping is not expected.
strings.note3: Book the Penguin Parade online, and note that photography is not allowed. The light at the Twelve Apostles is best in the afternoon. Queen Vic Market is closed Monday to Wednesday.
strings.note4: Laneways to see: Hosier, ACDC, Centre Place and Degraves. For street art, head to Fitzroy and Collingwood, and Sydney Road in Brunswick.
strings.note5: UV is high in summer, so wear sunscreen. Tap water is safe to drink.
strings.transit.name: myki
strings.transit.why_chosen: Covers trams, trains and buses. Trams in the centre are FREE (Free Tram Zone), and the daily cap is about 11 AUD.
